## What the object is called

There is one domain object with two names. `crimes` names it directly — finding `crime_00004`, **Cross-Language Concept Alias Drift** (`packages/api/billing/plans.py:10`, low severity, confidence 0.65):

> concept group "tenant" is named differently on each side of the boundary
> Python uses: team
> TypeScript uses: workspace
> preferred form for this group: "organization"

So: **`team` on the Python side, `workspace` on the TypeScript side**, one concept, 3 files. That's the rename.

## Every site

`crimes` enumerated 9 of them; I read the files to confirm and to pick up the one truncated as "…+1 more".

**Python — `team`** (`packages/api/billing/`)

| Location | Name |
|---|---|
| `routes.py:11` | `def get_team(team_id)` + route `GET /api/teams/{team_id}` |
| `routes.py:16` | `def create_team(payload)` + route `POST /api/teams` |
| `routes.py:21` | `def team_seats(team_id)` + route `GET /api/teams/{team_id}/seats` |
| `routes.py:26` | `def change_team_plan(team_id, plan)` + route `POST /api/teams/{team_id}/plan` |
| `plans.py:11` | docstring of `Plan` — "The tiers a **team** can be on" |

Note every handler also takes a `team_id` parameter — the identifier name renames too, and it's load-bearing in FastAPI because it must match the `{team_id}` path placeholder.

**TypeScript — `workspace`** (`packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts`)

| Location | Name |
|---|---|
| `:12` | `interface Workspace` |
| `:17` | `getWorkspace()` → `/api/workspaces/{id}` |
| `:22` | `createWorkspace()` → `POST /api/workspaces` |
| `:27` | `workspaceSeats()` → `/api/teams/:id/seats` |
| `:33` | `changeWorkspacePlan()` → `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan` (this is the "+1 more") |

Plus the filename itself — `workspace-client.ts` — and the module's header comment, which already documents the drift ("Calls the concept a 'workspace' throughout; the backend calls the same thing a 'team'").

## The trap: `team` is also a plan value

This is the thing that would break a find-and-replace. `crimes_00001` (**Cross-Language Type Drift**, high) shows the plan enum:

> `packages/api/billing/plans.py:10` — Plan declares [free, pro, **team**, scale]

`Plan.TEAM = "team"` at `plans.py:15` and `Plan.TEAM: 10` at `plans.py:22` are a *pricing tier*, not the tenant concept. A blind `team` → `organization` sweep renames a billing tier and changes a wire value customers are already on. Any rename must be symbol-scoped, not textual.

That collision is also the tiebreaker on which name to pick. **I'd take `crimes`' suggestion of `organization`**: `team` as the canonical name permanently overloads a live plan value, and `workspace` costs the same URL churn as `organization` without resolving anything.

## What else you'd have to touch

**The HTTP surface, which is already inconsistent.** The TS client isn't consistently on either name — two calls go to `/api/workspaces`, two to `/api/teams`. `crimes` caught both consequences:

- `crime_00005` (medium): `packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:23 — POST /api/workspaces` reaches a path no backend route declares. Currently a 404.
- `crime_00003` (medium): frontend sends `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`, backend declares `POST`. A 405, which as the summary notes "is easy to misread as a permissions problem."

Both are pre-existing bugs, but they mean the rename crosses the wire. Renaming the routes to `/api/organizations/*` is a public API break needing a deprecation window or an alias — that decision is upstream of the code change.

**A separate bug the rename will walk past.** `workspaceSeats` and `changeWorkspacePlan` take an `id` argument and then fetch the literal string `"/api/teams/:id/seats"` — `:id` is never interpolated. `crimes` matched these on the literal path so they didn't register as drift, but they're broken today. Worth fixing in the same pass since you're editing the lines anyway.

**The plan enum, which needs its own decision.** `crime_00001` is the only high-severity finding and is independent of the rename: Python has `[free, pro, team, scale]`, TypeScript has `[free, pro, enterprise]`. Shared: `free`, `pro`. Python-only: `team`, `scale`. TypeScript-only: `enterprise`. Three values one side will reject. Don't bundle this into the rename commit — but if you're introducing codegen or a shared schema to fix it, that's the same boundary work, so sequencing them together is reasonable.

## Blind spots in this analysis

Three things to be explicit about before you treat the file list as complete:

1. **`crimes` never read the manifests.** Coverage warnings report 3 `.json` files (`crimes.config.json`, `package.json`, `packages/web/package.json`) and 1 `.toml` (`packages/api/pyproject.toml`) matched no include pattern, "so no detector ever read them." Package names, module paths, and script entries may embed either name. Check them by hand.

2. **`blast_radius: 0` on all five findings does not mean "safe."** Coverage is `files_total: 3`. Nothing in this fixture imports anything else, so there are no in-repo importers to count. Real consumers — a database schema with a `teams` table, migrations, API docs, client SDKs — are outside the scanned set and invisible here.

3. **`test_gap: 1.0` on every finding.** There are no tests in the repo at all. A cross-language rename with zero test coverage has no safety net; the 405 and 404 above are proof that nothing currently catches boundary breakage.

## Suggested sequencing

I haven't changed anything. When you want to proceed:

1. Decide the canonical name (`organization`) and whether the URL change ships with an alias.
2. Fix the two route bugs and the un-interpolated `:id` first, so the rename lands on a working baseline.
3. Rename symbol-by-symbol, treating `Plan.TEAM` as off-limits.
4. Settle the plan enum separately — `crimes`' suggested action is "generate one side from the other, or share a schema," on the grounds that "keeping two hand-maintained copies in sync is the thing that already failed here."

One practical note: all five fingerprints key on file path and symbol (e.g. `cross_language_concept_alias_drift::packages/api/billing/plans.py::`). Renaming the files and symbols will re-key every one, so a post-rename `crimes diff` will show them as fixed-plus-new rather than as a clean improvement. Expect that churn and read past it.
